podcast.body: Co-written by Jerry Leiber and Mike Stoller, this song was initially conceived by them as a joke, comparing it to "Black Denim Trousers and Motorcycle Boots." It notably incorporates a "stop time blues riff" previously used in Muddy Waters' "Hoochie Coochie Man" and other Leiber and Stoller compositions. Despite the writers' initial skepticism about its suitability for Elvis, he performed it with such ferocity that it resonated with audiences and was chosen as the opening song for his 1968 "comeback special." "Either way, Elvis performs the song with enough ferocity that it sounded right to a lot of other people."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.body: This song was recorded during one overnight session and was a track "left over from King Creole," showcasing the stylistic range Elvis was covering in this period. "There was a Libra and Stolar Rucker left over from King Creole."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
